text:
Gabriel Landeskog won the Masterton and the Messier Leadership Award last season for coming back from a knee injury that cost him years. This season he gets to just be a hockey player again, and he's a good one: 8 goals and 14 points in 23 games on 15 minutes a night, on a line with Nazem Kadri and Nicolas Roy that The Denver Post says is starting to click.

The underlying numbers are better than the points. Colorado gets about 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, about seven points better than when he sits, and his team has scored 5.5 fewer goals than those chances deserve with him out there. That has cost him assists and usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey's caution is that he skates with very strong teammates, which flatters raw on-ice numbers.

The Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal pointed out that his five-on-five shot volume was way down early, then jumped in a three-game burst. That's the thing we'd watch. He scored three goals in two games right after it. A 33-year-old shooting more is a 33-year-old whose legs are fine.
